paper_title: Axion-Induced Patchy Screening of the Cosmic Microwave Background
suggested_experiment_name: CMB-S4 / Planck axion-photon coupling constraint from CMB spectral distortions
coupling_convention: g_agamma in GeV^-1, as plotted on y-axis (canonical axion-photon coupling)
notes: This is a PROJECTION paper forecasting sensitivity, not a measured exclusion limit. The paper forecasts that Planck+unWISE could probe g_agamma ≲ 3×10^-12 GeV^-1 for axion masses 2×10^-13 to 3×10^-12 eV via CMB temperature-LSS cross-correlation ⟨T^a g⟩. CMB-S4 could extend reach by ~order of magnitude. The data_points encode the mass range and best projected sensitivity as a horizontal line. The paper uses halo model to compute photon-axion conversion in magnetized plasma within large-scale structure, producing anisotropic CMB temperature and polarization distortions. Key observables: temperature auto-correlation ⟨T^a T^a⟩, polarization auto-correlation ⟨B^a B^a⟩, temperature-galaxy cross-correlation ⟨T^a g⟩ (most sensitive), and polarization-galaxy bispectrum ⟨B^a B^a g⟩. Confidence level 0.68 (1-σ) from Bayesian posterior. No local DM density assumption needed—this is a cosmological/astrophysical bound, not a haloscope experiment. | selector: figure_vision (sole candidate) | Vision: Figure 2 shows the exclusion region (blue shaded area) for axion-photon coupling g_agamma vs axion mass m_a. The lower boundary of this exclusion region (the constraint curve) has been traced. The x-axis spans from ~10^-14 eV to ~10^-10 eV in axion mass, and the y-axis spans from ~10^-13 to ~10^-8 GeV^-1 in coupling. The boundary shows a general downward trend (decreasing coupling with increasing mass) with some curvature.
